title: Fibrewise trivial lines are locally pulled back over a normal base
statement: Let $S$ be a normal scheme [def-pc-scheme], meaning every local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $p:X\to S$ be a smooth separated morphism of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] with nonempty geometrically connected fibres (each residue-field fibre stays connected after every field extension). Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. Let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Suppose that for every point $s\in S$ its tensor pullback $L_s$ to $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ is trivial, where $\kappa(s)$ is the residue field [def-weil-residue-field, def-pc-fibre-product, def-pc-module-pullback]. There is a Zariski open covering $\{U_a\}$ of $S$ and invertible modules $N_a$ on $U_a$ with $L|_{X\times_SU_a}\simeq p_{U_a}^*N_a$. No Noetherian hypothesis, section, group law, semiabelian hypothesis or uniqueness of these isomorphisms is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0BD7 (lemma-in-image-pullback) is the integral locally Noetherian generic-fibre result. The arbitrary normal-base, fibrewise formulation here is an agent-stated approximation/locality prerequisite; 0BD7 is not quoted as already proving the non-Noetherian extension. Smooth finite-presentation normal-family approximation supplies the intended reduction.

proof.text: Fix $s\in S$ and set $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$ for $R=\mathcal O_{S,s}$. By the normality hypothesis $R$ is an integrally closed domain; it is local. Form $X_T=X\times_ST$, with line $L_T$. Smoothness is preserved by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2), separatedness by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-base-change], and finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3). The same permanence statement (2) makes $X_T$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Its fibres remain nonempty and geometrically connected: for a field-valued point of $T$, the composite to $S$ factors through its image's residue field, and the fibre is the corresponding field extension of the original fibre. These identifications follow by applying the universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] twice. In local rank-one frames tensor pullback sends the frame to $1\otimes e$, so $L_T$ is invertible and the given fibre trivializations pull back to every such field-valued fibre [def-sc-invertible-module, def-pc-module-pullback].

source.place: Tag 0BD7, normal-base locality reduction; arbitrary-base localization written by the agent

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-normal-domain-smooth-family-models] to $X_T\to T$. Work on its directed tail, writing $T_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ and $X_i\to T_i$. These are normal integral Noetherian bases and smooth separated finitely presented families with nonempty geometrically connected fibres. The limit is the original family and the transition maps are affine. By [lem-trf-invertible-affine-limit-descent] there is, after increasing the starting index, an invertible module $L_i$ on $X_i$ whose pullback to $X_T$ is $L_T$. At every later stage put $L_j$ equal to its tensor pullback. This is invertible by pulling back rank-one frames [def-sc-invertible-module, def-pc-module-pullback].

source.place: Tag 0B8W, lemma-descend-invertible-modules (2); normal model input as cited

proof.text: Write $K=\operatorname{Frac}R$, $\eta_i=\operatorname{Spec}\operatorname{Frac}A_i$, and $X_{i,\eta_i}=X_i\times_{T_i}\eta_i$. Apply [lem-sbc-cartesian-family-generic-limit] to the systems from step 2. Its hypotheses hold: the base stages are integral qcqs, every $T\to T_i$ is dominant, all transition and comparison squares are cartesian, and the family components are qcqs. Thus $X_{T,K}$ is the limit of the qcqs $X_{i,\eta_i}$ with affine transitions. The map $\operatorname{Spec}K\to S$ factors through $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ at its image $t$: on an affine neighbourhood it is a ring map $B\to K$ with prime kernel $\mathfrak p$; the injection $B/\mathfrak p\hookrightarrow K$ extends to its fraction field $\kappa(t)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. Consequently the assumed triviality of $L_t$ pulls back to a specified isomorphism $L_T|_{X_{T,K}}\cong\mathcal O_{X_{T,K}}$; associativity of the fibre-product universal property and functorial tensor pullback give the identification [def-pc-fibre-product, def-pc-module-pullback]. Apply [lem-trf-fp-module-limit-isomorphism-descent] to the two fixed models $L_i|_{X_{i,\eta_i}}$ and $\mathcal O_{X_{i,\eta_i}}$. Both are finitely presented since locally they are free of rank one. It gives, at some later $j$, an isomorphism $L_j|_{X_{j,\eta_j}}\cong\mathcal O_{X_{j,\eta_j}}$, including its inverse. Only this generic-fibre trivialization is descended; no assertion that all fibre trivializations descend is needed.

source.place: Tag 01ZR, lemma-descend-modules-finite-presentation (2),(3); generic-fibre limit as in pione.tex Tag 0EZJ

proof.text: The smooth family $f_j:X_j\to T_j$ is flat by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. Each of its residue-field fibres is integral and nonempty by [lem-trf-smooth-connected-fibre-normal-integrality], applied to its nonempty geometrically connected fibres. Its source is Noetherian, hence locally Noetherian, as part of the model lemma in step 2. The normality, integrality and local Noetherianity of $T_j$ are supplied by the model lemma in step 2. Also $f_j$ is quasi-compact, since it is finitely presented. Step 3 supplies generic triviality. All hypotheses of [lem-sfb-normal-noetherian-generic-line-pullback] now hold, so $L_j\cong f_j^*N_j$ for an invertible module $N_j$ on $T_j$.

source.place: Tag 0BD7, lemma-in-image-pullback, all five hypotheses checked

proof.text: Pull this isomorphism back to $X_T$. Functoriality [def-pc-module-pullback] gives $L_T\cong f_T^*N$ with $N$ the pullback of $N_j$ to $T$. It is invertible, since rank-one frames pull back to rank-one frames. An invertible module on the spectrum of a local ring is trivial: by [def-sc-invertible-module] there is an open neighbourhood of the closed point on which it is free of rank one; this open contains some basic $D(a)$ through the closed point. Then $a$ is outside the unique maximal ideal, hence a unit, so $D(a)=T$. Thus $N\cong\mathcal O_T$ and $L_T\cong\mathcal O_{X_T}$.

source.place: Tag 0BD7, pullback conclusion; elementary local-ring rank-one argument

proof.text: Choose an affine open $V\subseteq S$ containing $s$ and use the directed system of affine neighbourhoods $W\subseteq V$ of $s$ in [lem-weil-pbc-local-ring-spec-limit-affine-neighbourhoods]. It has limit $T$, qcqs stages and affine transitions. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-over-limit], the system $X_W=X\times_SW$ has limit $X_T$ with affine transitions; take its starting stage to be $X_V$. Each $X_W$ is qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](2),(3), since $p$ is finitely presented and $W$ is affine. On the starting stage the two modules $L|_{X_V}$ and $\mathcal O_{X_V}$ are finitely presented (locally free of rank one). Their pullbacks to the limit are isomorphic by step 5. The isomorphism and its inverse therefore descend by [lem-trf-fp-module-limit-isomorphism-descent] to some affine neighbourhood $U_s$ of $s$. We obtain $L|_{X_{U_s}}\cong\mathcal O_{X_{U_s}}$. This argument uses the spectrum of the local ring, not an integral open neighbourhood of $s$.

source.place: Tag 01ZR, lemma-descend-modules-finite-presentation (2),(3), applied to the local-ring neighbourhood limit

proof.text: As $s$ varies these $U_s$ cover $S$. Take $N_s=\mathcal O_{U_s}$. Tensor pullback of the structure sheaf is the structure sheaf (the maps $b\otimes a\mapsto b\,f^\sharp(a)$ and $b\mapsto b\otimes1$ are inverse). Hence step 6 gives $L|_{X_{U_s}}\cong p_{U_s}^*N_s$, as required [def-pc-module-pullback]. If $S$ is empty take the empty covering. There is no requirement to glue the local isomorphisms or to choose them uniquely.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0BD7 combined with normal Noetherian approximation from pione.tex Tag 0EZJ and module limit descent, Tags 0B8W and 01ZR. The non-Noetherian local-ring reduction and neighbourhood assembly are agent-written.
